correctness.rationale: Direct signed-node calculation gives the claimed moment formulas. Gaussian Isserlis moments fix the true innovation variance. originality.rationale: The classical per-frame cubature moment formulas and sensitivity under rotation are not new; the finding classifies sharp attained innovation-variance extremes for all symmetric quadratic forms, proves no gaps between extrema, identifies the necessary-and-sufficient trace/Frobenius sign threshold and equality frames, and links these to unconditional actual-versus-reported MSE. Direct comparisons with the original 2009 rule, 2017 rotated-point paper, the 2024 nonlinear covariance framework and the 2026 compensation/gauge paper found no stated optimized spectral classification. Indexed searches did not reveal a complete duplicate; priority remains open to independent verification.
residual_risks: General formulas in 2017 and 2026 papers are close enough that an unindexed note may already derive the spectral special case; an independent priority check is needed.
The result concerns unconditional actual estimator MSE, not a pointwise conditional Bayesian posterior; using the latter terminology would misstate the theorem.
The 2024 motivating article has later revisions; original first-public-date evidence was checked at its arXiv record.

value.rationale: The invariant trace-to-Frobenius ratio gives an exact necessary-and-sufficient phase boundary for whether any cubature covariance-square-root frame can be calibrated. It distinguishes one-sided versus two-sided MSE reporting bias for the very same Gaussian prior, including an unbounded actual-minus-reported MSE family under fixed gain. This is a natural complete classification with practical diagnostic meaning, not merely routine positive-definiteness or a numerical example.
